prompt: The export endpoint needs a reliability fix in src/export-route.js. Keep interfaces exportRecords({ source, sink, maxBufferedBytes }) and createExportHandler({ source, maxBufferedBytes }); the default maxBufferedBytes is BUFFER_LIMIT_BYTES, which remains 64. A sink has write(string), end(), and once('drain', fn) and once('close', fn); write() returns false when it cannot accept more until a later drain, so wait for drain before another write or page fetch. sink.bufferedBytes counts bytes accepted but not consumed; a real response's writableLength has the same meaning. Never let that value exceed maxBufferedBytes after a write, when output does not fit the remaining space, and do not fetch another page while the sink is full. Empty pages are not end markers; continue fetching later pages. On sink close, stop later writes and fetches, call source.close(), and do not call sink.end(). Call source.close() after normal completion and after fetchPage throws. On a fetchPage error, preserve written bytes, append exactly {"error":"export failed"} plus a newline, and end exactly once. Set statusCode to 500 only when no record was written; otherwise preserve the existing status. Normal completion ends exactly once and writes no error record. Keep content-type application/x-ndjson and fast-reader bytes byte-for-byte unchanged, including empty pages; keep createPagedSource(pages), pagesFetched, and its closed state usable. Do not add dependencies or use real-time waits. Update relevant documentation or the changelog and add focused tests; all existing tests must continue to pass.

verdicts.note: The prompt describes the problem (backpressure, client closure, error handling) and the interfaces to use, but does not prescribe implementation methods or tool names. It specifies what behavior is required, not how to achieve it.

The prompt specifies the exact error message format, the byte limit (64), the interface contracts (write, end, once('drain'), once('close')), and expected behaviors for close, error, and normal cases. Hidden tests use these same contracts with a test Sink implementation matching the described interface.

The fixture exports BUFFER_LIMIT_BYTES (64) and the source/sink interfaces, but the existing test only covers basic happy-path output. No fixture comments, stubs, or docs reveal the backpressure, drain-waiting, or close-handling logic required by hidden tests.

A naive fix that only adds maxBufferedBytes parameter without proper drain waiting would fail the 'stalled sink never receives more than the configured buffered ceiling' test. Skipping client-close handling fails multiple close-related tests. The 16 hidden tests cover backpressure, close handling, error handling, and source lifecycle comprehensively.
